passages.scripture: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.

lines.text: Jesus is the Christ.
We need to be in Christ Jesus.
We are among those who are in Christ Jesus.
If we are in Christ Jesus, then we are not condemned.
There is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.

passages.scripture: For in Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit of life set you free from the law of sin and death.

lines.text: There is a law of sin and death.
The law of sin and death brings bondage.
We were enslaved to the law of sin and death.
However, now we are in Christ Jesus.
The Spirit of Christ Jesus is the Spirit of life.
The Spirit gives life in Christ Jesus.
The Spirit of life has a law.
The law of the Spirit brings freedom.
Because we are in Christ Jesus, the law of the Spirit set us free.
Now we are free from the law of sin and death.

passages.scripture: For what the law was powerless to do in that it was weakened by the flesh, God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin. He thus condemned sin in the flesh, so that the righteous standard of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

lines.text: The law of God was powerless to save us.
Our sinful flesh weakened the law.
God did what the law could not.
God sent His own Son.
God sent His Son in the likeness of sinful flesh.
God sent His Son as an offering for sin.
God condemned sin in the flesh through His Son.
God did this so that the righteous requirement of the law would be fulfilled in us.
We do not live according to the flesh.
Instead, we live according to the Spirit.

passages.scripture: Those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh; but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.

lines.text: Some people live according to the flesh.
These people set their minds on the things of the flesh.
Other people live according to the Spirit.
These people set their minds on the things of the Spirit.

passages.scripture: The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace, because the mind of the flesh is hostile to God: It does not submit to God’s law, nor can it do so.

lines.text: The mind of the flesh leads to death.
Whereas the mind of the Spirit leads to life.
The mind of the Spirit leads to peace.
The mind of the flesh is hostile to God.
The mind of the flesh does not submit to God's law.
The mind of the flesh cannot submit to God's law.

passages.scripture: Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.

lines.text: Some people are controlled by the flesh.
They are not controlled by the Spirit.
Those controlled by the flesh do not submit to God.
Those controlled by the flesh cannot do what God desires.
Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.
God is not pleased with them.

passages.scripture: You, however, are controlled not by the flesh, but by the Spirit, if the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.

lines.text: You are not controlled by the flesh.
You are controlled by the Spirit.
This is true if the Spirit of God lives in you.
We need to have the Spirit of Christ.
If anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.

passages.scripture: But if Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, yet your spirit is alive because of righteousness.

lines.text: Christ is in you.
And, therefore, because of sin, your body is dead.
However, because of righteousness, your spirit is alive.

passages.scripture: And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead is living in you, He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit, who lives in you.

lines.text: God has power to raise the dead.
God raised Jesus from the dead.
Our bodies are mortal.
Our mortal bodies are weak and can die.
But God’s Spirit lives in us.
If God’s Spirit lives in us, God will also give life to our mortal bodies.
God will give life to our mortal bodies through His Spirit.
The Spirit of God is living in us.

passages.scripture: Therefore, brothers, we have an obligation, but it is not to the flesh, to live according to it.

lines.text: Paul speaks to his brothers.
We are obligated.
Our obligation is not to the flesh.
We do not owe the flesh anything.
We are not required to live according to the flesh.

passages.scripture: For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

lines.text: We must not live according to the flesh.
If we live according to the flesh, we will die.
Instead, we must live by the Spirit.
If we live by the Spirit, then we put to death the deeds of the body.
If we put to death the deeds of the body by the Spirit, then we will live.

passages.scripture: For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.

lines.text: The Spirit of God must lead us.
We must be led by the Spirit.
If God's Spirit leads us, then God is our Father.
If we are led by the Spirit, then we are sons of God.

passages.scripture: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but you received the Spirit of sonship, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”

lines.text: We have received the Holy Spirit.
God's Holy Spirit is not a spirit of slavery.
When we were enslaved to sin, we lived in fear.
The Spirit of God does not return us to fear.
Instead of a spirit of slavery, the Holy Spirit is a Spirit of sonship.
We are adopted sons of God.
We are no longer slaves to fear.
We cry, “Abba! Father!” through God's Spirit.

passages.scripture: The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.

lines.text: The Spirit is the Spirit of God.
The Spirit Himself testifies.
The Spirit testifies with our spirit.
We are God’s children.
God is our Father.
The Spirit tells and confirms to us this is true.

passages.scripture: And if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ—if indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him.

lines.text: We are God’s children.
God’s children are heirs.
We inherit from God.
We are heirs of God.
We are co-heirs with Christ.
We are co-heirs with Christ if we suffer with Him.
And if we suffer with Christ, then we will be glorified together with Christ.

passages.scripture: I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.

lines.text: Paul considers our present sufferings.
These sufferings happen now.
In the future God will glorify us.
As a drop of water is to the oceans, even more so our sufferings cannot be compared to our future glory.
God will reveal this glory in us.
The glory that is coming far surpasses our present pain.
This future glory is beyond all comparison.

passages.scripture: The creation waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the sons of God.

lines.text: Creation expects.
Creation is waiting.
Creation waits with expectation.
Creation is waiting with eager expectation.
There are sons of God.
The sons of God will be revealed in the future.
Creation expects the sons of God to be revealed.
Creation eagerly expects this revelation.

passages.scripture: For the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of the children of God.

lines.text: God created everything.
God subjected creation to futility.
Creation did not choose this futility.
God subjected creation to futility for a purpose.
This subjection to futility was in hope.
Creation now suffers under decay and corruption.
Creation is in bondage to this decay.
God will set creation free.
God will free creation from decay.
God will bring creation into freedom.
This freedom belongs to the children of God.
This freedom is full of glory.
We hope for this freedom.
God subjected creation in this hope.

passages.scripture: We know that the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until the present time.

lines.text: All creation suffers.
All creation groans together.
All creation feels pain like a woman giving birth.
This pain continues until now.

passages.scripture: Not only that, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies.

lines.text: We have the firstfruits of the Spirit.
We groan inwardly.
We wait for our adoption as God’s children.
We wait for the redemption of our bodies.
We wait eagerly.

passages.scripture: For in this hope we were saved; but hope that is seen is no hope at all. Who hopes for what he can already see?

lines.text: We hope for adoption.
We hope for the redemption of our bodies.
God saved us in this hope.
If we already see something, how can we hope for it?
We can only hope for things we do not yet see.
Hope that we can already see is not real hope.
No one hopes for what he already sees.

passages.scripture: But if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently.

lines.text: We hope for things that we do not see.
We do not see these things now.
So we wait for them.
And we wait with patience.

passages.scripture: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.

lines.text: The Holy Spirit is God’s Spirit.
The Holy Spirit helps us when we are weak.
We do not know how to pray as we should.
The Holy Spirit prays for us.
The Holy Spirit intercedes to God for us.
The Holy Spirit speaks to God for us with groans.
These groans are too deep for words.
These groans are deeper than what words can express.
The groans of the Holy Spirit cannot be expressed by words.

passages.scripture: And He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.

lines.text: God searches our hearts.
God knows the mind of the Spirit.
The Spirit intercedes for the saints.
The Spirit prays according to the will of God.

passages.scripture: And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.

lines.text: God acts for those who love Him.
God works all things together for their good.
God called these people according to His purpose.
We know this truth.

passages.scripture: For those God foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.

lines.text: God foreknew everything before the foundation of the world.
God foreknew everything before all creation.
God foreknew all people that could and would be created or born.
God foreknew the choices all people could and would make.
God foreknew His chosen people.
If God foreknew us, then God also predestined us.
God predestined the people He foreknew.
The only begotten Son of God is Jesus.
God predestined that these people would become like His Son.
There is the image of the Son of God.
God chose that these people would be conformed to the image of His Son.
God did this so that Jesus would be the firstborn.
Jesus will be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters.

passages.scripture: And those He predestined, He also called; those He called, He also justified; those He justified, He also glorified.

lines.text: If God predestined us, then God also called us.
If God called us, then God also justified us.
If God justified us, then God also glorified us.

passages.scripture: What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?

lines.text: God is for us.
God is not against us.
And because God is for us, no one can stand against us.
We respond to these truths with confidence.
Because God is for us, we are secure.

passages.scripture: He who did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?

lines.text: Jesus is God's own Son.
God needed to give up and sacrifice Jesus to save us.
And God was willing to give up His own Son.
God gave Jesus up for us all.
God did not choose to spare Jesus from the cross, leaving us all to burn up like Sodom and Gomorrah.
God did not spare His own Son.
No! Instead, God gave His Son up for us - for our salvation.
All things were created through Jesus.
Jesus is greater than all things that are created.
If God gave us His Son, Who is greater, then God will also freely give us all things, which are lesser.

passages.scripture: Who will bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.

lines.text: God's elect are God's chosen people.
God justifies His elect.
Because there is nothing and no one greater than God, when God justifies, no one can bring a charge against God's elect.
God justifies and declares His elect righteous.
God justifies and declares His elect righteous and His word is absolute.
No one can accuse God's elect.
No one can say that God's elect is guilty of unrighteousness.

passages.scripture: Who is there to condemn us? For Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, is at the right hand of God—and He is interceding for us.

lines.text: No one can condemn us.
Christ Jesus, the Son of God, died for us.
And, even more, God raised Christ Jesus to life!
Christ Jesus now sits at God’s right hand.
Christ Jesus intercedes for us as our Great High Priest.

passages.scripture: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?

lines.text: Christ loves us.
No one and nothing can separate us from the love of Christ.
Trouble cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
Distress cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
Persecution cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
Famine cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
Nakedness cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
Danger cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
The sword cannot separate us from Christ’s love.

passages.scripture: As it is written: “For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.”

lines.text: We face death all day long for the sake of God.
People count us as sheep for slaughter.
The Scripture says this.
We face death and suffer because we belong to God.
Others see us like weak and helpless sheep.
Others are ready to slaughter us like sheep.

passages.scripture: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.

lines.text: We are more than those who conquered like Genghis Khan and Alexander the Great.
We are more than conquerors.
We are more than conquerors in all our troubles.
We are more than conquerors in all our distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger, and sword.
We are more than conquerors through Christ.
Christ loved us by laying down His life for us, His friends.

passages.scripture: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers, neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

lines.text: Death cannot separate us from the love of God.
Life cannot separate us from the love of God.
Angels cannot separate us from the love of God.
Rulers or principalities cannot separate us from the love of God.
Nothing in the present can separate us from the love of God.
Nothing in the future can separate us from the love of God.
No powers can separate us from the love of God.
No height can separate us from the love of God.
No depth can separate us from the love of God.
Nothing else in all creation can separate us from the love of God.
Paul is convinced of this truth.
The love of God is in Christ Jesus.
Christ Jesus is our Lord.
